title: Vesti on the unusual way he became a Mercedes Junior driver
excerpt:
Mercedes’ Third Driver Fred Vesti has shared an insight into the unusual way that he became a part of the squad’s Junior Programme, as well as reflecting on why he feels “deep in my heart” that there will be a seat for him on the F1 grid in the future.

Vesti was competing in his second season of Formula 3 in 2021 when he was signed up as a Mercedes Junior – a pathway that occurred after he found a way to quiz Team Principal Toto Wolff at an event away from the racetrack.

“I had followed Toto in Germany in Hockenheim,” Vesti explained on the latest episode of official podcast F1 Beyond The Grid. “I knew he was coming to a party. I was almost like a journalist at the red carpet.

“I stopped him at the red carpet and I asked him, ‘How do I become a junior driver with you?’ That was how I started the conversation with Mercedes. I just had this vision of being a Mercedes Junior and it could take me all the way to Formula 1, so yeah, it was a very different way of approaching a junior programme.

“I think he respects that a lot and I think he respects passion massively, and if he can see that you are motivated beyond anything he has seen before, I think that's where you make the difference. It wasn't easy getting signed by Mercedes at this point.

“One of the reasons why I really liked the Mercedes Junior Programme was actually because they only had a few drivers. They had George [Russell] and a couple of other drivers and that was it. So to be a Mercedes Junior driver is something very few people get to do.”

Since getting signed to the squad, Vesti – who went on to finish as runner-up in the 2023 Formula 2 championship – became a reserve driver from 2024 onwards, which has seen him participate in FP1 sessions for the team as well as undertaking plenty of simulator work.

The role also means that Vesti works closely with Russell and Kimi Antonelli, with the Dane admitting that, when it comes to the difference in their driving styles: “For me as the third driver in the sim, I sort of have to do both.

“I have to balance both drivers because we are equally using their data. I think Kimi, one thing that he does quite a lot is he sends in a lot of speed into the corner, which, with this car, it seems to work really well. George in some ways backs it up a bit more, focusses on the exit, but it's not as simple as this because it changes weekend to weekend, corner to corner.”

And while Vesti is currently focused on supporting Mercedes’ main drivers each race weekend, the 24-year-old is still chasing his own F1 dream, a goal that he feels confident he can achieve.

“It's a very unforgiving job as third driver,” he explained. “You are helping making champions but it's not yourself. Obviously, I've had my own dreams of racing in Formula 1 since I was a kid and that dream is still very much alive. The team sees me as a Formula 1 driver.

“Sometimes they say, ‘Fred you're not a rookie, you have done so much testing, you are so prepared for a Formula 1 seat’, so I'm living and breathing like a Formula 1 driver. That's the trust I have from the engineers first of all.

“They need a lot of trust in the driver that they lean on if that [stepping in for Russell or Antonelli] would happen, and it's taken me some good time, some years to become the driver I am today and to be ready for that scenario.

“I'm working with the best engineers, the best drivers in the world and I'm really improving rapidly as a driver towards Formula 1. My dream is to be on the grid, winning races, fighting for championships in Formula 1 and that's what I wake up thinking about every morning.

“I'm working so hard for it. I have this feeling so deep in my heart that there is a seat for me, and I am so hungry and ready to do anything to achieve that goal. The goal is a Formula 1 seat and I can feel it's coming.”

title: What tyres will the teams have for the United States GP?
excerpt:
Next up on the 2026 F1 calendar is the United States Grand Prix, held at Austin's Circuit of The Americas – and tyre suppliers Pirelli have confirmed the compounds that will be in use throughout the weekend.

For this year's event, the C2 has been selected as the hard compound, with the C3 as the medium and C4 as the soft. This marks a change from last season, when Pirelli brought three non-consecutive compounds (the C1, C3 and C4) for what was a Sprint weekend.

The usual Grand Prix format is in place this time around, so drivers will get two sets of the hard tyre (marked white), three sets of the medium tyre (marked yellow), and eight sets of the soft tyre (marked red), as well as access to the green intermediate tyre and the blue full wets, should they be required.

An extra set of softs is reserved for those who reach Q3 in Qualifying, while all drivers must use at least two different slick compounds during the race, providing the track is dry.

"The Austin circuit, which is 5.513km long, features a mix of high-speed corners, rapid direction changes and slower sections that demand strong traction," reads Pirelli's weekend preview. "To be competitive, teams must combine good straight-line speed with efficient aerodynamic load through the more technical sections, an aspect that becomes even more important with the current generation of Formula 1 cars.

"From a tyre perspective, COTA places demands on both axles. In the first sector, characterised by fast corners and direction changes inspired by some of Europe’s great circuits, the front tyres will be placed under particular stress. In the third sector, meanwhile, the numerous acceleration zones out of slow corners will tend to generate thermal degradation primarily on the rear tyres.

"The asphalt surface is not particularly abrasive. A section of the circuit between Turns 9 and 11 was resurfaced earlier this year. However, the ageing effect on the remainder of the track continues to be significant and contributes to high wear levels. Tyre wear, rather than graining, could therefore prove to be one of the key factors over the weekend. During last year's event, several tyres reached very high wear values.

"Track grip is generally good, aided by the support categories, including the Porsche Carrera Cup North America, which has been supplied by Pirelli since the start of this year. Track evolution, on the other hand, has traditionally not been among the most pronounced on the calendar.

"From a strategic standpoint, the presence of the C2 as the hard compound could favour long stints, offering teams a solid option for what is likely to be a one-stop race. However, the high temperatures that typically characterise the Texan weekend must also be taken into account, as they could increase degradation and open the door to alternative strategies."

title: How Williams entered the Marvel Universe
excerpt:
Williams unveiled a special Doctor Doom-inspired livery earlier this month as part of their ongoing collaboration with Marvel, replacing their usual blue with the villain's trademark black and green colours.

The striking design made its debut at New York Comic Con, where the team showcased a specially-liveried FW48 show car alongside superhero-inspired race suits and exclusive merchandise.

Taking inspiration from one of Marvel's most recognisable villains, the car was displayed as part of an immersive experience celebrating the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film, with the collaboration bringing together Formula 1 and one of the world's biggest entertainment franchises.

While neither Alex Albon nor Carlos Sainz will race with the design, fans attending this weekend's United States Grand Prix can get a closer look at the livery at the Williams Fan Zone in Austin.

Williams assemble!

The collaboration began back in April, when Williams announced that Albon, Sainz and Team Principal James Vowles would be making their Marvel Comics debut in a special one-shot comic book, Iron Man: Racing Towards Doom.

The story sees the Williams trio face an altogether different challenge to their usual F1 rivals, with Doctor Doom threatening to disrupt the racing season.

Fortunately, they have a little help from some familiar faces. Iron Man, Black Widow and Captain America join the team as they attempt to prevent the supervillain from carrying out his plans.

Written by Ethan Sacks, with artwork by Greg Land, the 32-page comic brings the drivers into the Marvel Universe, complete with superhero action, dramatic illustrations and plenty of F1 references.

Crossovers between sport and superhero comics may seem unusual, but according to Dr Miriam Kent, Lecturer in Film and Media at the University of Leeds and author of Women in Marvel Films, the relationship between superheroes and sport is nothing new.

"We can look back to the history of superhero publishers working with sports teams or featuring famous athletes – going back to the '50s, '60s and '70s, even,” she explains. “Superhero comics have always had an odd relationship to the 'real world', but it's not unusual to find references to public figures or sports teams. The Thing in Fantastic Four is a fan of the New York Jets, I believe."

Dr Kent also pointed to Sacks' experience writing comics for another major entertainment franchise.

"The writer [of the Williams comic] has a strong reputation for working on tie-in comics for Star Wars. He'll be an old hand at extending universes across media – even if those universes are part of our real world."

The comic is set for its wider US release on October 21, just before the Grand Prix in Austin.

9 times superhero movies made it onto the F1 grid

Bringing Marvel to the paddock

Williams' partnership with Marvel has extended well beyond the pages of their comic book story, with special-edition covers released throughout the 2026 season.

Beginning with an activation at the Miami Grand Prix, which featured Marvel artwork and a giant comic book cover photo opportunity, the collaboration has travelled to several races on the calendar.

Limited-edition covers have celebrated Grands Prix including Monaco, Great Britain, Spain and Singapore, with further editions for the United States and Las Vegas giving fans the chance to build their own collection.

The team have even introduced a Marvel-themed digital badge for their Williams ID members, offering exclusive digital assets to mark the partnership.

For Dr Kent, there is also a natural connection between Formula 1's technological innovations and the superhero genre, which has long explored the possibilities of advanced machinery and engineering.

"I think there is something to be said about Marvel affiliating itself with the cutting-edge technology that's involved in F1. Again, there is a history of this – going back all the way to Iron Man, Marvel had a partnership with [car company] Audi. Tony Stark drove an R8 in the film, and Audi featured the character in its own marketing.

"The superhero genre has long been concerned with what it means to push the limits of technology, where the boundaries are between humans and technology. A lot of the appeal is the tech superheroes have access to. So in a way, cars and superheroes make sense."

A superhero takeover at Comic Con

The collaboration took centre stage at New York Comic Con, held from October 8-11, where Williams took their place among some of the biggest names in comics and entertainment.

Alongside the Doctor Doom-inspired show car, visitors could explore a dedicated Williams experience within Marvel's exhibition space, featuring comic book artwork, superhero-inspired race suits and interactive displays.

Visitors could pick up one of 2,000 comics printed with an exclusive New York Comic Con cover, while race-worn suits and boots belonging to Albon and Sainz were also offered for purchase.

Fans also had the opportunity to enter a competition to win one of the special Marvel-inspired race suits, bringing a little superhero style to their own wardrobes.

Next stop: Austin

For fans who missed the New York unveiling, the special livery is making another appearance in Texas this week.

The Williams Fan Zone, located in downtown Austin, will display the Marvel-inspired show car between October 19 and 24. There'll also be a special Austin edition of the comic book available to purchase.

The Fan Zone will also feature appearances from Albon, Vowles, reserve driver Luke Browning and 1996 World Champion Damon Hill, alongside interactive racing experiences.

title: Why Red Bull and Audi’s floor stay trick is banned for 2027
excerpt:
A clever regulation loophole used this season by Red Bull and Audi has been outlawed as from next season. The ‘floor stay’ loophole gets around the regulation limiting the radius angle on the edges of the sidepod, to give a much more aggressive shape for a cleaner airflow along the sidepod undercut as it travels to the rear of the car.

To understand how this works requires an explanation of the bodywork radius regulations. These stipulate the maximum permitted radius angles of the various bodywork panels at their corners and edges.

title: FIA president disputes Middle East 'risk' as F1 decision looms
excerpt:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has voiced confidence that F1 will finish its season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Uncertainty looms over the final two rounds of the season due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Earlier in the year, F1 postponed the events in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain, with the former ultimately cancelled while the latter moved to Malaysia.

Other racing categories have opted to steer clear of venturing to that region to close out their championships, however F1 is still holding out for the possibility of staging its final two rounds as originally scheduled.

Ben Sulayem has insisted he has no concerns over safety, should they opt to stage the events.

"One thing I would say; I have my children there. I'm here, but they are there. You think I would leave them there, and I am here now with you?

"Also, you have to be sensible in this and say, 'are we going to have an issue?'

"What you read in the media is actually different than we have there. We read, and we see the TV, [and say] where is it?

"We don't have that really. Otherwise, why would I stay there? Why would I leave my family?

"But does this mean that there is nothing going to happen? I can't predict this. I can only tell you today that there is nothing, and the two races are going to happen.

"I don't think the FIA staff would be more important to me than myself and my family. But if I am there, it means I feel secure about it. But we don't know."

Recent reports have suggested that the Dakar Rally could move away from Saudi Arabia in January next year.

While Ben Sulayem insisted that it is safe to venture to Qatar and Abu Dhabi, when speaking about the Dakar Rally, he asserted the FIA is putting personnel safety as its highest priority.

"We will never take our staff or drivers or any officials to a place where we feel it is risky. No way."

Article continues below.

FIA 'ready' for Imola alternative

Should F1 ultimately not opt to race in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to close out the campaign, a replacement race has been touted.

It would see F1 venture back to Imola in Italy to close out the season and would mark the first time in almost three decades that the sport had its final race in Europe.

When asked if FIA would be ready to head to Imola, Ben Sulayem replied: "Of course, FIA is always ready.

"I told the GM to have another ready team from the FIA if there was nothing going on, but maybe some of the governments say, 'you cannot travel'. So what do we do?

"I mean, if everybody is there and then the teams are there and the FOM is running it, and suddenly we say, 'Oh, we cannot have our race director, we cannot have our stewards.

"No. You have to be ready, and you have to have another team ready, just in case."

title: Kimi Raikkonen smashes longstanding F1 records on date of greatest triumph
excerpt:
Kimi Raikkonen claimed two ancient F1 records in emphatic style on this day, 21 October, in 2018, at the United States Grand Prix.

Eleven years to the day after securing his only F1 drivers' championship, Kimi Raikkonen marked 21 October with another slice of history, winning the 2018 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas.

In doing so, he became the oldest grand prix winner since Nigel Mansell in 1994 and the record holder for the longest gap between F1 victories.

The Finn, then 39 years old, had not stood on the top step since the 2013 Australian Grand Prix, a run of 114 races without a win.

That figure eclipsed the previous mark of 98 races set by Riccardo Patrese, who went winless between the 1983 South African Grand Prix and the 1990 San Marino Grand Prix.

Raikkonen started second on the grid behind Lewis Hamilton's pole-sitting Mercedes but made the most of Ferrari's race pace in Austin, converting it into a lights-to-flag-style victory while team-mate Sebastian Vettel fought back from adversity to finish fourth, behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, who rounded out the podium.

The result denied Hamilton, who needed to outscore Vettel by eight points, the chance to clinch his fifth drivers' title that weekend.

[Article continues below]

Driver

Kimi Räikkönen

Finnish

Years in the wilderness

The five-and-a-half-year gap between Raikkonen's wins told its own story of misfortune and misalignment.

His 2013 triumph in Melbourne came for a Lotus squad whose finances deteriorated so badly by that November that the Finn was forced to sit out the final two rounds of the season.

A return to Ferrari for 2014 brought no respite: the F14 T was hamstrung by a pull-rod front suspension layout that never suited Raikkonen's preference for sharp front-end response.

From 2015 onward, as Mercedes dominated the hybrid era, Raikkonen's chances were further squeezed by team strategies that frequently prioritised Vettel's title bids.

Patrese's own seven-year drought, by comparison, had been a product of unreliable and uncompetitive machinery through stints at Alfa Romeo and a declining Brabham outfit between 1984 and 1987, before he finally ended it at Imola in 1990 after joining Williams during its switch to works Renault power.

For Raikkonen, the win in Austin would be the last of his 21 career victories, a fitting final flourish on a date that already carried the weight of his 2007 drivers' title with Ferrari at Interlagos.

title: Qatar circuit boss delivers readiness update as double header nears
excerpt:
The CEO of Qatar's Lusail International Circuit has made it clear that preparations are in full swing to host MotoGP and Formula 1 next month, despite the ongoing tense regional backdrop.

The ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran, combined with Houthi missile and drone strikes across the Arabian Peninsula, has already disrupted the 2026 motorsport calendar, contributing to the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian GP and the relocation of the Bahrain event to Malaysia earlier this month.

A ballistic missile strike hit the Saudi Aramco headquarters complex in Dhahran on October 13, roughly 160 kilometres across the Persian Gulf from Lusail, while maritime strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and aerial strikes on regional transport hubs have raised fresh concerns over potential airspace closures and freight delays.

Against that backdrop, Lusail's ability to deliver a smooth, secure double header carries added significance, with F1 and the FIA maintaining that the Qatar GP will go ahead as scheduled on November 29, while keeping Italy's Imola circuit on standby should conditions deteriorate further.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has said the governing body regards Qatar and Abu Dhabi as sufficiently secure to host races and would not send paddock personnel or drivers into areas of unmanaged danger, while Qatari authorities have reaffirmed that the country is safe and that it expects to host both events as planned.

The three-week gap between the two rounds, with MotoGP taking place on November 4-6, means the venue faces a tight turnaround, but with work continuing across grandstands, hospitality areas and the wider event infrastructure despite the backdrop of ongoing instability elsewhere in the Middle East.

Lusail International Circuit CEO Abdulaziz Ali Al-Muhannadi said preparations for the events are progressing as planned.

"We are looking forward to welcoming the world back to Lusail International Circuit in November for two of the most anticipated events on the international motorsport calendar, just three weeks apart," said Al-Muhannadi.

"Our preparations are nearing completion, with our teams focused on ensuring that every aspect of the venue is ready to deliver an exceptional experience for fans, as we do every year."

title: 2026 F1 United States Grand Prix - Austin weather forecast
excerpt:
2026 F1 United States Grand Prix - Austin weather forecast

The upcoming United States Grand Prix at Austin will feature friendly conditions for F1 drivers - and provide a potential overtaking aid.

The weekend in Texas is currently forecast to be dry, with temperatures in the high-20s Celsius region, possibly tipping over to the low 30s on Saturday.

There are currently two rain cells of note appearing on weather radars, with one being to the south in the Gulf of Mexico, but is not expected to move inland from Galveston Bay up to Austin.

The other is trapped by the Rocky Mountains and will be present to the northwest of Texas throughout the weekend. Although some leading-edge cloud might drift towards the Texan state capital, the main rain cells will not.

Crucially, drivers can expect an overtaking aid in the form of a headwind into the iconic raised Turn 1 braking zone.

The straight-finish straight and approach to Turn 1 at Austin run to the south-east, which is where the wind is set to come from throughout the weekend, thus meaning a head-wind will be present, which will allow drivers to brake later into Turn 1 and try to pass rivals.

For the other major overtaking spot, at Turn 12 at the end of the back straight, which runs north-east to south-west, drivers will be greeted with a crosswind from left-to-right in the braking zone.

title: FIA introduces strict new rule to shut F1 budget cap loophole
excerpt:
The FIA has introduced a brand-new article in the operational regulations for the upcoming F1 season. This is intended to prevent teams from using workarounds to have staff work on the Formula 1 project while they are officially part of a different department.

The FIA has introduced a brand new article into the operational regulations aimed at stopping Formula 1 teams from using back-door routes to keep staff effectively working on their F1 project while officially sitting under a different division.

Formula 1 teams have operated under a budget cap since 2021, limiting how much they can spend developing a faster car and forcing them to prioritise where that money goes.

There are a handful of exceptions, including driver salaries and the pay packets of the three best-remunerated senior figures at each outfit, but beyond that, salaries are included, and teams have found it far harder to simply hire more people in the search for small performance gains.

Several teams run separate divisions that work on projects outside Formula 1 entirely, though suspicion has lingered for some time that data could still be passed across to benefit the F1 operation. Red Bull has its Advanced Technologies arm, Aston Martin runs Performance Technologies, and Mercedes has its Applied Sciences division.

To prevent information from those divisions from actually making its way back to the F1 team, the FIA has decided to introduce an entirely new article into the operational regulations from the 2027 season.

The article, titled Physical and IT Segregation Between F1 Activities and Non-F1 Activities, requires teams to strictly separate their F1 operations from non-F1 activities, both physically and digitally.

That means staff will no longer be able to simply share workspaces and IT systems, and access to technical data will need to be tightly controlled.

Restrictions will also apply to shared facilities. Certain equipment, such as simulators, wind tunnels and test rigs, can still be used by both groups, but in principle not at the same time.

Teams will additionally be required to manage and log access rights, allowing the FIA to check that the rules are being followed.

[Article continues below]

Stricter rules on data and staff

The FIA will also be given explicit powers to check compliance through on-site inspections and forensic IT audits. Teams will not be permitted to get around the rules by swapping technical information via messaging apps, external storage devices, outside service providers or intermediaries.

From 1 January 2027, they will also be required to keep records of access rights and digital audit trails, so the governing body can verify compliance retrospectively.

The separation goes beyond simply keeping workspaces apart. The exchange of digital results and technical information will also be bound by strict conditions.

In certain cases, information from F1 staff may be passed to employees working on non-F1 activities, but only under specific conditions and with the required approval and documentation. The reverse transfer is not permitted.

The FIA has also set conditions for staff moving between F1 and non-F1 activities. Depending on the direction of the move, mandatory periods will apply during which they cannot carry out certain work or access relevant systems and data.

Through these measures, the FIA wants to stop teams exploiting the boundaries between different activities to indirectly share technical knowledge or resources. Responsibility for actually enforcing the separation lies with the teams themselves.

Article F6 is intended to tighten oversight of the divide between F1 and non-F1 activities, contributing to a fairer application of the sport's financial and technical regulations.

The key question now is how much teams running these kinds of external divisions will need to change their working practices to fall in line with the new rule.

title: Honda to reach major F1 milestone at 'demanding' US Grand Prix
excerpt:
Honda will become just the fifth F1 engine manufacturer to reach the milestone of 500 grand prix entries at this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

From its first entry at the 1964 German GP, Honda engines have been entered into a further 498 races, with the half-millennium coming up in Austin, Texas, in the Japanese manufacturer's latest venture into grand prix racing, with the Aston Martin squad.

Although it is Honda's 500th race entry, it is not Honda's 500th race start, with the 'missing race', as ever, being the 2005 United States Grand Prix at Indianapolis.

Honda was one of the Michelin teams that day which peeled off into the pits at the end of the formation lap, therefore meaning Jenson Button and Takuma Sato were officially credited with 'Did Not Starts'.

Honda will join Ferrari, Renault, Mercedes, and Ford-Cosworth in reaching 500 entries, with BMW sixth on the list, despite not having competed in grand prix racing since its 2009 withdrawal.

Looking ahead to the weekend, Honda's trackside general manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara spoke of the "privilege" Honda faces.

"The United States Grand Prix in Austin is always a special event, with a fantastic atmosphere and passionate fans," he said.

"This year, we have the privilege of celebrating 500 races in Formula 1, which brings more excitement and pride to the weekend.

"The Circuit of the Americas is a demanding circuit that combines fast and flowing sections with heavy traction zones.

"After the Singapore Grand Prix, our power unit and trackside staff travelled to HRC Sakura in Japan to review the last three events and prepare for another triple-header.

"Our power units have been fully serviced and are ready for Austin, where we will give it our utmost with the package we have."

title: Red Bull share 'wish' over Max Verstappen demands: 'His input is massive'
excerpt:
Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies has addressed the role Max Verstappen plays in development at the Milton Keynes-based team.

Laurent Mekies has praised the "massive input" Max Verstappen provides to Red Bull's development process, whilst admitting the team cannot always move as fast as its four-time F1 drivers' champion would like.

The Red Bull team principal's comments come after a dramatic turnaround in the RB22's competitiveness, culminating in back-to-back victories for Verstappen in Sepang and Singapore.

Red Bull began the current campaign as much as 1.5 seconds off the pace, hampered by chassis setup limitations and early aerodynamic shortcomings on the RB22.

Verstappen himself said after the season-opener in Australia that the deficit was split evenly between the chassis and the new Red Bull-Ford power unit.

The Dutchman had repeatedly flagged handling imbalances and unpredictable platform shifts that undermined his confidence on corner entry, along with problems managing bumps and kerbs, issues he again raised around the Hungarian Grand Prix when balance inconsistencies were hurting his long-run pace.

Matters shifted significantly with a comprehensive upgrade introduced at the Baku City Circuit, featuring a reworked floor, revised diffuser channelling, reshaped sidepods and new engine cover surfacing.

The package targeted the car's awkward trade-off between low-speed mechanical grip and high-speed stability, and it has since helped carry Verstappen to victories in Malaysia and Singapore.

Verstappen's 'technical sensitivities' are a 'massive help' for Red Bull

Asked about Verstappen's role in shaping that development direction, Mekies did not downplay his significance.

"His input is massive," the Frenchman told media, including RacingNews365. "You are absolutely right in saying that his technical sensitivities are outstanding.

"Probably without any equivalent, and therefore, yes, he does [have active influence on the recent progress].

"He has that capability to pinpoint what is limiting performance. Unfortunately for us, it doesn't mean that we have a fix for it when it tells us what the problem is.

"But at least it tells us what the problem is, and it's a massive help for the team."

Mekies explained that the relationship between Verstappen and his engineers hinges on honesty, even when it is not always comfortable.

"We do it in a way where we are always very direct and transparent with each other and constructive, even if it comes with emotion sometimes," Mekies said.

"And it's a massive boost for the chassis development and a massive boost for the power unit development.

"We wish we could provide solutions faster sometimes, but it's part of the game."

title: Kimi Antonelli handed 'really tricky' warning as first title-clinching opportunity awaits
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli can become world champion this weekend, but it will not be easy!

Kimi Antonelli has been warned that the United States Grand Prix could prove "really tricky" if Mercedes fails to get on top of the upgrade package that has left the team guessing since Malaysia, according to Jolyon Palmer.

Antonelli arrives at Circuit of the Americas holding a commanding 102-point lead at the top of the drivers' championship, with the first opportunity to seal the title awaiting him this weekend. But the Mercedes driver's form has been complicated by an aerodynamic upgrade introduced in Sepang that the team has struggled to fully understand.

Mercedes brought a revised package to Malaysia aimed at improving downforce efficiency, and Antonelli used it to qualify in the top three and lead that race. But the update produced an unpredictable balance through Singapore, where the team ran split specifications between its two cars in an attempt to isolate the problem, keeping Antonelli on the new parts while George Russell reverted to the older package.

Asked whether Antonelli can win both the race and the title in Austin, Palmer told the F1 Nation podcast that Mercedes itself remains in the dark.

"I really don't know because Mercedes don't know at this stage. I think that's where we're at with them," said Palmer.

"So I expect them to run this upgraded package again, which they put on the car for Malaysia. They didn't understand whether it was better or worse, although they suspected it was worse. And then they split the cars for Singapore.

"They felt like they learnt something with Antonelli's car through the weekend, and I'm expecting them to probably both go with the upgraded package, but at least Kimi to stick with it.

"And we will see then if what they learnt in Singapore can mean that they start on the right foot for Austin."

United States GP offers 'room to push'

Palmer believes the nature of the Circuit of the Americas, a permanent facility with far more run-off than Marina Bay, could work in Antonelli's favour even if the car's window remains narrow.

"Good news with Austin is it's a permanent racetrack," added Palmer. "There's margin for error. There's room to push the limits. Part of the weekend [in Singapore], Kimi was feeling like the car was quite difficult to drive.

"It was in a narrow window, and obviously in Singapore, you can't afford to get it wrong, or you're in the barriers, and he sort of found that out in that Baku weekend.

"So I think Austin will suit him a little more, maybe a bit more like Malaysia, where he was able to throw caution to the wind and actually had an okay performance, qualifying in the top three and leading the race.

"And we will then see if Mercedes can finally unlock what they still think is the true potential of this car. And if they do, he can win. If they don't, I think it'll be really tricky for him still."

title: F1 breaks into unexpected market with 'inspired' new product and partnership
excerpt:
Formula 1 has announced the release of an "inspired" new product, a camera, to kick off a partnership with Leica.

F1 and Leica Camera have launched a special-edition Leica Q3 43 Formula 1 camera, the first product to emerge from a new licensing partnership between the sport and the German optics manufacturer.

The Leica Q3 43 Formula 1 Edition has been priced at 9,950 US dollars, 7,300 British pounds and 8,500 euros, and will be sold through Leica Stores, the Leica Online Store and specialist retailers.

The camera's design draws directly on motorsport. A non-slip microvelour covering modelled on a racing steering wheel wraps the body, while carbon fibre, a material not traditionally used in Leica products but a mainstay in motor racing for combining low weight with high rigidity, forms the visible structure on the handgrips and thumb rests. A Formula 1 logo sits on the top plate and lens cap.

Leica has also developed an exclusive colour profile for the camera, delivering higher contrast and richer saturation to capture the atmosphere of the track and paddock.

The look is accessible through the Leica FOTOS app and can be applied live while shooting, appearing in the viewfinder rather than only during post-processing. The same app transfers images and video to mobile devices.

Part of a wider push

The camera is the latest in a run of consumer licensing deals struck by Formula 1 beyond the racetrack.

The sport has signed agreements covering board games with Hasbro, building toys and collectables with Lego and Mattel Hot Wheels, trading cards with Topps, and book publishing with Dorling Kindersley.

title: Exclusive: Red Bull commit to major F1 overhaul in bid to win back titles
excerpt:
Red Bull technical director Pierre Waché has explained just how much of the RB22 machine will be carried over into the 2027 RB23, in an exclusive RacingNews365 interview.

After a slow start to the season, Red Bull has transformed its car into a race-winning machine, with Max Verstappen claiming victory in Sepang and in Singapore, with an upgrade in Azerbaijan unleashing performance from the car.

Work is firmly underway on designing the new car for the 2027 season, with Red Bull expected to start the new season strongly and carry over its momentum into the second year of the regulations.

Although the 2026 titles are now firmly out of reach for Verstappen, Isack Hadjar, and the team, 2027 marks a strong opportunity to carry the newfound momentum over.

Detailing just how much of the RB22 will be carried over, Waché explained that "close to nothing" will make it to the RB23.

"There are some modifications to the regulations, and we have plenty of limitations on the car - and I'm sure others have different limitations," Waché exclusively told RacingNews365 when asked how much of the RB22 would carry over to 2027.

"It is not good for the [cost] cap, so we try to transfer not as much; it is not good for the budget cap, but we try to make plenty of new parts on the car.

"More or less close to nothing will transfer [to 2027], because there are plenty [of areas] we think we have identified we can improve.

"[These are] in terms of packaging, aerodynamics, and mechanical, and we will transfer some stuff, but it will be a very small amount, like the gearbox and chassis will be different."

title: Lando Norris reveals 'bias' as new status confirms F1 weight
excerpt:
Lando Norris believes his new status in F1 has afforded his voice extra weight.

Lando Norris has explained how he is "biased towards drivers and fans" in key GPDA meetings, where his new status as world champion carries extra weight.

The Grand Prix Drivers Association is the effective trade union of F1 drivers and meets to discuss topics of the day and to represent the drivers' views on these topics as a united force, as opposed to all 22 drivers voicing their own opinions independently of each other.

On the current grid, George Russell and Carlos Sainz serve as driver directors, with former F1 racer Alex Wurz the chairman. In the past, the likes of Michael Schumacher, Sebastian Vettel, and Fernando Alonso have all served as directors.

Norris is just one of four world champions on the current grid, with the others being Alonso, Lewis Hamilton, and Max Verstappen.

As a member of this rare group of senior drivers, Norris believes his voice has been given added weight in discussions, which is "cool", as he explained that his only "bias" in the meetings is to advocate for improving matters for drivers and the viewing fans.

[Article continues below].

© XPBimages

Norris explains new F1 weight

"I mean, the GPDA is obviously represented by a few drivers, but the input that they put in is our input as drivers," Norris told media, including RacingNews365.

"So it's not that they just decide what they want to decide; they decide what we decide as a collection of drivers.

"Obviously, I'm part of that, and maybe people listen to my voice more now than previously, and that's something that just comes with, I guess, the credit of winning the world championship.

"But it's not something I think you expect, but it is just respect, I think, at the end of the day, and that's a cool thing to earn through your career, but the GPDA is everyone.

"So it's not just me, but of course, if I have input, my input is just as valuable.

"I still want the best for the sport. I'm never biased. I would say anything I do, I do for what I want the sport to be.

"I'm biased towards drivers and fans more than rules and things like that."

title: Toto Wolff issues 'full-on' Red Bull prediction as major question looms
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has made it clear that Red Bull will be in what he expects to be a "full-on" battle for championship honours in F1 next year, with a question mark also hanging over Mercedes' recent upgrade package.

Toto Wolff has praised Red Bull's turnaround this season after Max Verstappen won back-to-back grands prix in Sepang and Singapore, with the Mercedes team principal predicting a "full-on" fight between the leading teams, including the Milton Keynes-based squad, next year.

Verstappen's consecutive victories hauled Red Bull out of what had been shaping up as its first winless campaign since 2015, with the RB22 and its Ford-developed power unit struggling to find their window for much of the opening 14 rounds.

That changed with a major aerodynamic upgrade introduced at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which transformed the car's operating range and set up the double win that followed.

It marks a significant achievement in Red Bull's first season as a power unit manufacturer, a venture team principal Laurent Mekies previously likened to climbing an "Everest" given the scale of catching established manufacturers Ferrari and Mercedes.

Wolff, speaking to media including RacingNews365, was generous in his assessment of the Milton Keynes-based squad's progress.

"Really, you need to take your hat off to what Red Bull has done this season, how they have developed the car and how it's all come together as a package," Wolff told media, including RacingNews365.

"And then you put Max Verstappen in the car, and when he feels that this thing is driving like he wants it to drive, then you know these are the results.

"He's been by far the quickest guy [in Singapore]. He's been the quickest guy in Kuala Lumpur."

[Article continues below]

Mercedes response awaited

George Russell went further, declaring Red Bull "the team to beat" after Verstappen's pace across three contrasting circuits.

Mekies welcomed the assessment, pointing out the pace had shown up on "different track types" and should translate elsewhere on the calendar.

Kimi Antonelli, Russell's team-mate and the drivers' championship leader, was more guarded, suggesting Mercedes simply has not extracted the maximum from its own new package rather than conceding Red Bull has leapt ahead.

Wolff made clear the response from Brackley will hinge on the recent upgrade, which Mercedes struggled to extract the most out of as Verstappen roared to victory in Malaysia and Singapore.

The Austrian was adamant, however, that Red Bull will be in the battle for supremacy next year, alongside his team, Ferrari and McLaren.

"Let's see when our upgrade hopefully starts to work, and lands in a place where we think it should be, whether we can be competitive against him," Wolff added.

"But one thing is for sure: next year it's a full-on fight between the teams, and Red Bull is part of that."

title: The Red Bull figures who will ultimately decide Liam Lawson F1 future
excerpt:
Liam Lawson is continuing to await a decision on his F1 future with Racing Bulls.

Racing Bulls finds itself in a common F1 problem of finding out that 'three into two' won't go, with three drivers vying for two 2027 race seats.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are the incumbents, with F2 title contender Nikola Tsolov eager for promotion to grand prix racing, and his title rival Rafael Camara set to join the grid with Haas next season.

Lindblad's impressive rookie season has all but earned him an extension into a second season, with it likely to be Lawson vs Tsolov for the second seat.

RacingNews365 takes a look at the figures that will be central to deciding whether Lawson or Tsolov get the nod.

A change from Marko

Previously, the arrangement of who filled the four Red Bull-backed seats on the F1 grid was overseen by Red Bull GmbH advisor Helmut Marko and former Red Bull team principal and CEO, Christian Horner.

Indeed, it was Marko who pushed for Lawson's promotion to Red Bull for 2025, something Horner has claimed his in memoir left him "uncomfortable."

But with both Marko and Horner firmly out of the picture, the decision-making committee at Red Bull has changed.

There are six key players involved in the decision for the driver line-up at Racing Bulls, with this being the only unconfirmed team on the grid. Mercedes has not yet officially confirmed Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, but they will not be dropped, and whilst Oliver Bearman's extension at Haas is not yet official, it is a matter of when, not if.

Those on the Red Bull-Racing Bulls decision-making committee are in the table below, listed in alphabetical order.

The Red Bull figures who will ultimately decide Liam Lawson F1 future

Name

Position

Peter Bayer

CEO of Racing Bulls

Mark Mateschitz

Minority owner of Red Bull GmbH

Laurent Mekies

Red Bull F1 Team Principal and CEO

Oliver Mintzlaff

Red Bull GmbH CEO of Corporate Projects

Alan Permane

Team Principal of Racing Bulls

Chalerm Yoovidhya

Majority owner of Red Bull GmbH

Aside from Peter Bayer and Alan Permane, whose Racing Bulls team Lawson races for, a key figure is Oliver Mintzlaff (below with Permane).

He serves as the CEO of Corporate Projects for Red Bull GmbH, and thus has direct control over both the company's F1 teams.

Whilst the final decision will be taken by the shareholders, Chalerm Yoovidhya and Mark Mateschitz, they will act on the recommendation provided to them by Mintzlaff, Bayer, and Permane.

Yoovidhya owns 51% of the shares of Red Bull, with his father creating Krating Daeng - with Red Bull being closely related to the original drink designed for rural labourers. Mateschitz, the son of the late Dietrich, owns the remaining 49% of shares.

title: Sergio Perez brands major F1 rule 'unfair' ahead of crucial vote
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has called the F1 cost cap "unfair for smaller teams" as Williams boss James Vowles tries to make changes to the spending restrictions.

At a meeting of the F1 Commission next month, a vote is scheduled to be held on Vowles' idea to introduce a sliding scale for the cost cap as opposed to the flat-rate imposed on all teams at the moment, with those finishing lower down the constructors' standings receiving more spending power than those at the top.

A similar scale was introduced for the Aerodynamic Testing Regulations (ATR), where wind-tunnel and CFD time was gradually reduced the higher a team finished up the standings for the next season - with a mid-season update.

Cadillac is one of the teams believed to be in favour of Vowles' idea, with the Williams chief requiring six votes, including his own, for the change to be made for 2027 - with this date being in mind so the changes could fully bed in for the expected 2030 return to V8 engines.

Perez, who has experience of both ends of the cost cap having driven for Red Bull between 2021 and 2024, feels it is "unfair" on those teams at the bottom of the standings.

"No," Perez's reply began when asked by media, including RacingNews365 if the team had more upgrades planned.

"We are obviously a new team and a small team. I think the cost cap these days is a lot more unfair for smaller teams because when I was at Red Bull, for example, we used to bring upgrades pretty much every weekend.

"You never heard anything about the cost cap. It was all about performance, bringing, and throwing everything you could.

"But when you are in smaller teams, because they're not as efficient and they don't have their methods as clear, you end up overspending so much more money.

"So actually, the cost cap, instead of making it closer between teams, creates these massive gaps that we currently have on the grid."

[Article continues below]

Is Vowles likely to get his change through?

The F1 Commission is a body containing all 11 teams, the FIA, F1, and other voters.

Vowles requires the consent of six teams to change the rules for 2027, including his own, but looks set to fail.

Alpine, Aston Martin, Audi, and Cadillac all look set to vote with Williams, but this only brings Vowles to five, with Ferrari, McLaren, Mercedes, and Red Bull all understood to be against.

This leaves Haas and Racing Bulls.

However, both are understood to be against the idea, with Racing Bulls chief Alan Permane recently stating his opposition, therefore rendering Vowles' plans as struggling to pass.

He could try again in 2027 for a 2028 introduction, when he would only require four votes.
